---
title: 26. Multiplying big numbers
---

{% include menu.html %}

*Create a program to multiply very big integer numbers.*

The support for big numbers is built-in: the `Int` class allows arbitrary precision. You do not have to do any extra work. You just take the numbers and multiply them, as shown in the example (numbers should be written on one line, and without spaces, of course):

```raku-static
my $a =
    83274938493874832658327320948349783624839479683297463483
    72463286948532460989746932849382643928497328656329878246
    39847823659328476832647392847836539843928645384329463287
    53924837825643824302487637563724384782374803284710339876;

my $b =
    23849389520394874100302935470340851094327485279287346539
    23423599234023403275324932549011093234845878830238479823
    38497357295682768498203985784582309487857450938547650202
    34958452087248754293875293059257429584375683984543867549;

say $a * $b;
```

Run the program and check the result :-)

```
$ raku multiply.rk
1986056445427346134608816461674104817709618067621430859563207

6325794905191426940032936330373925095492741926233188581116641
016422307707317083924
```
